pr_title: Move Tado zone state handling into upstream python-tado library

Thanks for the review, I'll circle back to this once I finish fixing some issues with `elkm1`

Thanks for the effort!

What's the benefit from writing state vs calling update? Does this also make sure that the front-end is refreshed when you make a change in the app?

I'll try to test it out later today or tomorrow.

Calling update will try to update the entity if it's polling and then write state. Since we know we're not polling, we can just call write state directly, which means we skip 1 await, making it slightly faster :)

> That is where we landed on after this discussion here [#33195 (comment)](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/33195#issuecomment-604125010)

Don't know that I've ever said before, but I think mine's a tado v2 smart ac controlling a fujitsu ac unit that also heats :)

What do you folks have, and does it support a "true" auto heat/cool mode for your device, ie heats if it's too cold and cools if it's too hot based on the set temperature? (Mine doesn't - in Tado it only offers heat, or cool, so setting a smartschedule means choosing one of those two modes for each time block).

Am I right in saying that @michaelarnauts description of expected behaviour is that changing the temperate in auto creates the tado overlay (taking it out of smartschedule), but leaves the hass thermostat still in auto?
To me, that's not auto, because the tado is no longer running the smartschedule (If i've misunderstood the comment then please let me know).

However, if my tado supported an actual auto mode with my AC unit, then simply setting the temperature in auto mode and leaving the unit to work out what it should do would make perfect sense...

For me, changing the temperature in the tado app sets up the manual overlay retaining the heat or cold mode from the smart schedule.

That might mean there's possibly a semantic issue of how the tado modes should map to the hass thermostat modes/controls based on the capabilities that the Tado unit has with any particular AC unit.

For my unit, it makes logical sense that:

tado smart schedule = thermostat auto
tado heat overlay = thermostat heating
tado cool overlay = thermostat cooling
tado off = thermostat off

But for a tado supporting an actual auto heat/cool mode, the following would make more sense:

tado smart schedule = thermostat auto
tado auto heat/cool overlay - thermostat auto
tado heat overlay = thermostat heating
tado cool overlay = thermostat cooling
tado off = thermostat off

Right now though the temperature change in auto mode is back to forcing a "cool" overlay for me.

I'm still better off than I was, in that I now now specific heat and cool modes which I can use, rather than the original which only presented a single heat/cool mode that only ever ran cooling on my tado. 

Hope the rambling makes sense I keep revising what I've written). Appreciate that with a system like tado with such a broad spectrum of device coverage and variation in what it presents there might not be a perfect fit for everyone...

Things are quieting down a bit here so I should be free to do more testing if required...

@bdraco @michaelarnauts 

The more I think about this the more it makes sense - especially if @michaelarnauts has a true auto heat/cool mode on his tado - setting a temperature on auto **_is_** an overlay for that setup, whereas for me setting auto mode means a return to a non-overlay smartschedule mode.

It could also mean that the unintended change in mode to cool for me when setting temperature in auto mode is a side effect of not having an auto heat/cool overlay mode supported on my tado to change into, so it's defaulting to cool and reporting that change back to hass (as opposed to incorrectly _setting_ Cool, which is what I assumed it was doing...)

Just grasping at straws...

I only have a heating mode, not cooling. The overlay mode of tado is a way to make a change to the temperature while allowing to fallback to auto after a while.

When you want to keep your temperature fixed, you need the MANUAL overlay. This is configurable with the fallback parameter.

Now, from my point of view, changing the temperature from within the auto mode leaves the auto mode, since you are overriding the temperature.

The heat and cool scenario described a different auto mode, one where you change the temperature, but you let the device figure out if it needs to cool or heat. Isn't that the heat/cool mode you need? I suppose changing the temperature from auto, should switch to that mode (if available). The component can't know if you want heating only or cooling only. Actually, why do you want to restrict to heating only or cooling only, to save energy costs?

Reading above posts again, aren't we saying all the same? The only change needed is to have auto switch to heat/cool if it is available or to heat or cool otherwise, right?

> I only have a heating mode, not cooling. The overlay mode of tado is a way to make a change to the temperature while allowing to fallback to auto after a while.

Ah! Does that mean you have the Smart Thermostat? I have the Smart AC Control, so maybe the default for each may be different internally, with yours being Heat, and mine being Cool ? And if it switches back to default mode that might be why mine keeps switching to Cool...

> When you want to keep your temperature fixed, you need the MANUAL overlay. This is configurable with the fallback parameter.

In the tado app, would that be a change with the indefinite run time (that says "until you cancel")?
(The options I get when I change the temperature are that it default for an preset duration (2hrs for me), slide further for a duration ha increases in 15min blocks, "until next time block", or "until you cancel"

> Now, from my point of view, changing the temperature from within the auto mode leaves the auto mode, since you are overriding the temperature.

That's what I thought you meant :) And on a device where you can _only_ do one thing (ie Heat!) that makes sense since you've no other modes that you could change to...
 
> The heat and cool scenario described a different auto mode, one where you change the temperature, but you let the device figure out if it needs to cool or heat. Isn't that the heat/cool mode you need? I suppose changing the temperature from auto, should switch to that mode (if available). 

Agreed, although the auto heat/cool mode isn't available on my tado system (ironically, it is available if I use my AC remote). My tado only gives me Heat, or Cool within the smart schedule and when selecting a manual temperature. That's why in a multi mode system, it makes sense to me that auto maps to scheduled, and heat or cool map to the non auto heat and cool modes. In a system with only one mode there's only scheduled temperate, or overridden temperate.

> The component can't know if you want heating only or cooling only. 

Also agreed, so potentially saving a last active state reported might hold what it was last doing (ie heat, or cool) and use that to set the mode when the temperature is overridden.

>Actually, why do you want to restrict to heating only or cooling only, to save energy costs?

Not at all... Actually it's a very convoluted niche answer involving the fact my AC unit sets the vanes at a specific angle whenever the mode changes - one angle is set when it switches to cool mode, another angle when the mode changes to heat. On my unit, whenever you _switch_ to heat, the vents point straight down.
Sadly due to the position of my AC unit, pointing straight down means it blows heat directly onto another fixed appliance that then starts to overheat and fails.
 
I can change the vanes with the AC remote, and it remembers that set position even if the AC unit switches between active or idle, or off, but only changes when the _mode_ changes.

So for me now, changing the temperature in auto forces the mode to cool, maybe because mine is an AC Controller rather than a heating thermostat (I'm currently heating because it's still cold here). I then have to change the mode back to heat, which resets the vanes, and If I'm not around to find the AC remote and repoint the vanes I kill another appliance. Bit of a downer.

> Reading above posts again, aren't we saying all the same? 

Yep! I think we are!

> The only change needed is to have auto switch to heat/cool _if it is available_ or to heat or cool otherwise, right?

Yeah, and as you mentioned before the component can't know if it should be heat or cool, so saving a last active state reported might be the way to sensibly "assume" the correct mode and use that to set the mode when the temperature is overridden.

I indeed have the Smart Thermostat. Note that I don't have an AC in my house, and it is not common to cool your house here in Belgium. We typically only have central heating, so my assumptions on the usage of AC might be wrong. I do have an AC in my car, and that's how I look at the behaviour :)

So you have an really specific use case. I'm more thinking about the general usage of air conditioning units. I imagined that the heat/cool mode was something that every AC unit has (like the AC in my car) and is considered the default mode. I just set the target temperatures, and it figures out itself if it needs to heat or cool, based on the current temperature. I think some thermostats even have two target temperature settings, a low and a high. If the measured temperature drops below the low, it starts heating, if it rises above high, it starts cooling. 

I'm not sure if this is something how people use this, I guess one would always want to use heat/cool.

If we remember the last mode, things will work out for everybody I guess, as long as you used heat/cool before.

It just seems a bit "magic" to remember the last mode. If you accidentally put the AC to heat, put it back to auto, and you then want to cool down your house by lowering the target temperature, it will switch back to heat and won't cool your house?

I think your specific use case is better handled with an automation that sets it to cool always. Now, thinking about it, I don't see the relation between the heat/cool mode and the direction of the vents. Is that maybe a bug at the Tado side?

Just noticed this is merged PR, discussions should happen on an issue. Feel free to open one, but I'm still wondering if your use case with the vents isn't due to a Tado issue, and could be better solved with an automation.

> So you have an really specific use case. I'm more thinking about the general usage of air conditioning units. I imagined that the heat/cool mode was something that every AC unit has (like the AC in my car) and is considered the default mode. I just set the target temperatures, and it figures out itself if it needs to heat or cool, based on the current temperature. I think some thermostats even have two target temperature settings, a low and a high. If the measured temperature drops below the low, it starts heating, if it rises above high, it starts cooling.

Yep, my AC unit has Auto (heat/cool depending on set temp), heat only, and cool only (and off, but let's ignore that for the moment).
However, my Tado unit only recognises Heat, and Cool, and not Auto/Heat&Cool, so it doesn't offer me the "just set the temperate and it'll run auto".

> I'm not sure if this is something how people use this, I guess one would always want to use heat/cool.

In an ideal world yes!, Except for my pesky appliance overheating becuase of the vane settings - definitely my niche use case.

> If we remember the last mode, things will work out for everybody I guess, as long as you used heat/cool before.
> It just seems a bit "magic" to remember the last mode. If you accidentally put the AC to heat, put it back to auto, and you then want to cool down your house by lowering the target temperature, it will switch back to heat and won't cool your house?

Yep, that's why to me (originally) mapping auto to smartschedule (and removal of the overlay) makes sense. Putting the unit back in auto returns control to the Tado and it sets the mode based on the schedule, so no danger of the wrong heat or cool mode.

What mode to select when overriding comes down to whether the tado reports Heat/Cool differently to Heat Only and Cool Only.
If it does makes the distinction and heat/cool is available, that can be a distinct saved last state and also avoids wrong mode scenarios. If not available, then the scheduled tado mode can _only be_ ether heat, or cool, and preserving that can't result in a wrong mode.
Problems occur if heat/cool mode is available on the tado, but it only reports as heat or cool depending on what it was last doing...

If I remember rightly, the original component had Auto, Heat/Cool, and Off.
@bdraco's changes removed the Heat/Cool and put in separate Heat and Cool modes - which suited me better as they mapped to what my Tado was presenting.
So I guess the component should have all of them, Auto, Heat/Cool, Heat, and Cool - although maybe then have to decide whether hass auto == heat/cool, or auto == smartschedule/nooverlay

> I think your specific use case is better handled with an automation that sets it to cool always. 

I'm not sure I understand. "Cool always" is what I'm trying to avoid...

> Now, thinking about it, I don't see the relation between the heat/cool mode and the direction of the vents. Is that maybe a bug at the Tado side?

Oh this isn't a tado thing at all, it's a "feature" of the Fujitsu AC unit. The unit I have defaults the vane position on mode change to be helpful - in Cool, the vents points sideways to blow cold air across the room since cold air sinks, and it'll cool the room faster that way. In heat mode, it blows the air straight down for the exact same opposite reason - it'll heat the whole room faster since the hot air will rise, and avoids pooling the hot air at the top of the room...
So whenever the tado changes mode between heat or cool, the AC unit resets it's vane positions.
That's the same behaviour if I change modes with the original AC remote. Change modes and the vanes reset. It's utterly beyond the scope of the integration, but it is the reason why changing the mode incorrectly messes things up for me. Purely selfish. :)

> Just noticed this is merged PR, discussions should happen on an issue. Feel free to open one, but I'm still wondering if your use case with the vents isn't due to a Tado issue, and could be better solved with an automation.

Yeah, sorry, this was originally all in #32294 which got closed and merged to here...

The vents on my AC unit aren't controlled by the tado at all, other that as a side effect of changing the mode between heat or cool, and that takes me back to the original issue - changing the temperature on the card while in auto mode switches my tado to Cool regardless of what mode is running...

issue_context.title: Tado Smart AC incorrectly switches to 'Cool' mode if temperature changed.

Relevant Section:
#Default Handling
To set an override, the tado° cloud API requires a full setting (hvacMode, targetTemperature, fanspeed, swing) and a termination condition (operationMode, timerDuration). If only some of the properties are set, the binding fills the missing pieces automatically. It tries to keep the current state wherever possible.

If parts of the setting are missing, then the currently active zone setting is used to fill the gap. Only if the setting is not compatible with the requested change, then hard-coded defaults are applied.

hvacMode is set to HEAT for heating and hot water, and set to COOL for AC
targetTemperature for heating is 22°C / 72°F, AC is set to 20°C / 68°F and hot water to 50°C / 122°F
fanspeed is set to first supported value, for example AUTO
swing is set to OFF, if supported
If the termination condition is missing, the binding first checks if an override is active. If that is the case, the existing termination condition is used. An existing timer, for example, just keeps running. In case the zone is currently in smart-schedule mode and thus doesn't have a termination condition, then the default termination condition is used, as configured in the tado° app (settings -> select zone -> manual control on tado° device).

Just did a very quick test, and yes, you can be affected, but you can work around it by chaining together the service calls.

Calling climate.set_temperature forces mine into cool mode even if I specify _hvac_mode: heat_ in the service call.

But if I then call climate.set_hvac_mode explicitly I can specify heat or cool and it sticks.

So if using service calls in an automation/script for your schedule, set the temperature as one action, then set the hvac mode as the next action to correctly set the mode you want.

If you're using the front end card control, click the heat or cool icon first, and then set the temperature (although if you're already showing as in the mode you want, you're ok).

Behaviour might be slightly different for you, because a lot of it depends on the capabilities of the unit you've got it connected to and I think that affects the capabilities declared by the integration.

Hope this helps, and it would be great if you can confirm the behaviour you're seeing.
